author: GameSpot YouTube
text:
NOUGH: Beyond Lies of P - Video Documentary Trailer
Following consecutive award wins for Lies of P and its DLC, the camera turns from the glare of the stage to the quiet of the studio — the space where NOUGH Studio is preparing its next title. In place of applause comes a heavier question: "Can we make something better than Lies of P?"

The name NOUGH comes from "Not enough" — enough, minus the e. It starts from the belief that they are never quite enough.

This film shows how that relentlessness actually works. Nough Live, where the Director plays the latest build live for the entire studio at every milestone to share progress; and Game Day, where everyone plays the game themselves to judge whether it's actually fun. There is only one standard here: would we, as players, be satisfied with this game? Because they see themselves as gamers before developers, nothing is considered finished until every team member finds it genuinely fun.

The film carries one message: the developers' silence was never an empty space — it was time quietly spent building toward what comes next.

"We won't disappoint you. We promise. This isn't a lie — it's the truth."

This film contains no information about the next title — no genre, no name, no release window. Instead, it captures the time between the glow of past success and the reveal of what comes next: a period that looks like silence but is in fact the most intense stretch of all. Retrospectives that revisit past glory are common; footage that captures a studio still in development is not. It shows why a studio that has already proven itself keeps examining its own shortcomings, and continues to hold itself to a standard no one asked for. This is a record of that process, that pressure, and the beliefs and philosophy that define NOUGH.

text:
Spider-Man: Brand New Day vs. Insomniac Games
In an interview, actor Tom Holland and director Destin Daniel Cretton spoke about how the Spider-Man games from Insomniac influenced Brand New Day, specifically with how Spidey lands a knockout blow on his enemies.

“A lot of the action,” from the games inspired Holland, “A lot of the finishing moves. I was actually playing the game last night. For me, a lot of those finishing moves, a lot of our stuff was influenced by that stuff.”

Cretton added that Holland’s love of the games was shared by many of the stunt performers in the film, who brought screenshots of Spidey’s finishers to the writer’s room as they wanted to pull off those moves in real life. 

“A lot of the action designers and stunt people we had were huge gamers,” Cretton said. “They were able to experience things in those games that made them excited, and they would just screengrab the moves they really liked and bring them into the writers’ room and show it to me. And then we’d be like, ‘Yeah, that’s sick. Let’s try to figure out how to do that for real.'”
